terms.definition: A closed plane figure made of three or more line segments meeting only at endpoints.
A polygon with all sides congruent and all interior angles congruent.
An angle formed inside a polygon by two consecutive sides.
An angle formed by one side of a polygon and the extension of an adjacent side.
A segment joining two nonconsecutive vertices of a polygon.
A quadrilateral with both pairs of opposite sides parallel.
A parallelogram with four right angles.
A parallelogram with four congruent sides.
A parallelogram with four congruent sides and four right angles.
A quadrilateral with a pair of parallel sides called bases.
A trapezoid whose nonparallel legs are congruent.
A quadrilateral with two distinct pairs of adjacent congruent sides.
In a trapezoid, the segment joining the midpoints of the legs; its length is the average of the bases.
An angle formed by a base of a trapezoid and one of its legs.
Angles at consecutive vertices; in a parallelogram they are supplementary.
Angles at nonadjacent vertices; in a parallelogram they are congruent.
To divide into two congruent parts.
The ratio of vertical change to horizontal change between two points.
A coordinate formula for segment length derived from the Pythagorean theorem.
A coordinate formula that averages endpoint coordinates to locate a segment midpoint.
An angle whose vertex is the center of a regular polygon and whose rays meet consecutive vertices.
The perpendicular segment from the center of a regular polygon to a side.
The total length of a figure's boundary.
Breaking a complex figure into simpler figures whose measures can be combined.
A requirement or limit that a mathematical design must satisfy.
A property or set of properties strong enough to guarantee a classification.
A classification structure in which a figure can belong to a more specific class and all broader parent classes.
